title: Feature cost ownership & lifecycle — hiring coupler
content:
Purpose:
Quick, lightweight playbook to map feature-level cost ownership across the product lifecycle and tie hiring cadence to pricing triggers. The idea: attribute marginal inference and platform costs to feature owners, build a small proforma that captures ramp, and attach clear price/headcount trigger rules so GTM and Eng know when to hire or pause.

Context / why now:
- We're seeing uneven token growth across features (conversational assistants >> reranking).
- Team asks: which hires are justified by feature revenue, and what pricing delta would avoid a hire?
- Finance needs a compact tool that product/eng can use when planning sprints/approvals.

High-level approach (one-pager):
1) Cost attribution: split direct inference cost + shared infra by feature using a token-weighted allocation plus a small fixed feature tax (for infra metadata, logging, storage).
2) Lifecycle bands: Early, Growth, Mature. Each band has expected CVR/monetization and expected token intensity.
3) Hiring coupler: map 3-month rolling token velocity to hiring + pricing triggers.
4) Sensitivity scenarios: run price +/-10%, +/-20% and token elasticity -0.4 to -1.0 to estimate revenue and unit econ impact.

Key assumptions (editable cells in linked sheet):
- Average inference cost per token (GPU+ops): $0.000045 baseline (region-weighted).
- Shared infra overhead per feature (monitoring/logs): $1,200/month (divided by active features).
- Average fully-burdened IC cost: IC2 $12k/month, IC3 $18k/month, Eng Manager $28k/month.
- Onboarding lag: new hire contributes 50% output in month 1, 80% in month 2, 100% at month 3.
- Pricing elasticity by feature bucket: assistant -0.6, rerank -0.9, embeddings -0.4.

Compact proforma (example for "Search Assistant" feature):
- Baseline monthly tokens: 250M tokens
- Baseline price per 1k tokens: $0.60 (customer-facing) -> monthly revenue: 250k * $0.60 = $150,000
- Inference cost: 250M * $0.000045 = $11,250
- Allocated infra + fixed feature tax: $1,200 + shared slice $2,000 = $3,200
- Gross contribution before labor: $135,550

Headcount demand model (rule-of-thumb):
- 0.5 FTE per +200M tokens/month for assistant during growth band (includes SRE+obs+feature eng fractional effort).
- Hiring trigger = sustained 12-week rolling velocity > 220M tokens/month AND projected unit margin < 40% after ramp.

Example headcount table (compact) for Search Assistant (baseline -> 6-month plan):
Role | Existing FTE | Needed at +40% token growth | Monthly comp burden
Product PM | 0.5 | 0.5 | $9,000
Feature Eng | 1 | 1.5 -> hire +0.5 | $9,000 per added FTE
SRE (shared) | 0.2 | 0.4 -> fractional +0.2 | $3,600
Observability Eng | 0.0 | 0.2 -> fractional +0.2 | $3,600
Notes: hires are fractional across features; we recommend prioritizing fractional contractors for the first +0.5 FTE.

Pricing sensitivity sketches (baseline price = $0.60 per 1k tokens):
Scenario A (price -20% -> $0.48): elasticity -0.6 -> token demand +12% -> tokens = 280M; revenue = 280k * 0.48 = $134,400 -> revenue down 10.4% vs baseline; contribution margin falls ~6–8 pts.
Scenario B (price +10% -> $0.66): elasticity -0.6 -> token demand -6% -> tokens = 235M; revenue = 235k * 0.66 = $155,100 -> revenue up 3.4%; contribution margin improves by ~4–6 pts.
Observation: for assistant-type features elasticities imply small price increases can improve margin; price cuts are risky and require offsetting unit cost reductions (quantization, batching).

Hiring vs pricing tradeoff decision matrix (decision authority suggestions):
- If projected margin after forecasted hires < 30% -> require approval from Head of Finance + Product Director.
- If projected hires can be deferred by a price increase <= 10% (and customer impact tolerable) -> prefer pricing lever + A/B test for 8 weeks.
- If velocity is spiking (>40% growth over 8 weeks) and latency/SLA risk present -> immediate hire (fast-track) with 6-week contractor buffer.

Trigger automation (implementation notes for product/eng):
- Weekly job writes 7d and 90d rolling tokens per feature to finance sheet (linked).
- When 90d velocity > trigger, an automated Slack alert to #finance-ops and feature owner (templated message with delta and suggested action).
- Jira ticket template created: FIN-HIRE-REQ (links to proforma snapshot).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we include an explicit cost-of-capacity buffer for bursty features (e.g., 95th percentile GPU hours)? I lean yes, but need SRE input on sizing. (@Jonah Li).
- How to treat multi-feature shared customers (single invoice): attribution vs. uplift capture. Suggestation: attribute proportionally by measured token usage per feature per customer; mark a 5% reconciliation tax.
- How to calibrate elasticity by product vertical (B2B vs consumer)? We have coarse numbers; need to run controlled price A/Bs on low-risk cohorts.

Next steps (2-week sprint):
- (Finance) finalize proforma sheet and permissioning (week 1).
- (Eng) add weekly token exports and 90/7d metrics (week 1).
- (Product) pick a candidate feature for a small price experiment to validate elasticity (week 2).
- (All) reconvene after 2 full weeks of metrics and iterate thresholds.

Quick links and artifacts:
- proforma sheet (editable): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1abcXYZ-feature-cost-proforma
- related Confluence explainer: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/FIN/Feature+Cost+Ownership+Model
- Jira: FIN-442 (build token export + alerts)

Notes to self:
- Keep the first rollouts conservative; we can be opportunistic with pricing but document external comms and support runway for customers who cannot tolerate changes.
- Capture any non-linear infra costs (e.g., model variants, on-demand GPUs) as separate line items in the sheet so they don't get hidden in the unit cost cell.
